title: EHR Preferred Language: Capture, Route & Fix
summary: Learn how to capture preferred language in the EHR, separate interpreter need, route language access, fix inaccurate data.
body_markdown:
###


Preferred language is the language a patient wants to use for healthcare communication. It should be stored as structured data and kept separate from interpreter preference and, when useful, written-language preference.


###


No. Preferred language and interpreter need answer different questions. A patient may prefer a non-English language but not want an interpreter for every encounter, or may want interpretation only for certain types of care.


###


Compare EHR language values with interpreter-use logs, repeated language changes, and patient-reported interpreter preference. Reconfirm the value with the patient rather than inferring it from staff perception of English proficiency.


###


It can help drive routing when the EHR and interpretation workflow are integrated. The stored language can be passed into the interpretation workflow or used to preselect the language, with staff confirmation before the session begins.


###


The language a patient prefers for conversation may differ from the language or format that works best for written instructions. Keeping the fields separate reduces errors in discharge materials, portal communication, and patient education.
